chunk_findings.detail: When `launch="auto"` and ddflow is running from a source checkout, the Docker branch can still be selected: if `uvx` and `ddflow-mcp` are not on `PATH` but `docker` is, the condition `launch == "auto" and not shutil.which("uvx") and not shutil.which("ddflow-mcp") and shutil.which("docker")` is true and `_launch_entry` returns the Docker entry with the default `ghcr.io/OWNER/ddflow:latest` image. chunk_findings.detail: `has_legacy_block` treats the legacy marker strings as a block whenever they appear anywhere in the file (`LEGACY_BEGIN in text` and `LEGACY_END in text`), and `block_body` slices between their first occurrences. `block_spans` deliberately ignores markers that are not whole line-start lines, so an adopted project whose `AGENTS.md` merely documents the markers, e.g. a line containing `` `<!-- DDFLOW:BEGIN (managed — edits inside this block are overwritten) -->` `` followed later by a line containing `` `<!-- DDFLOW:END -->` ``, has no managed block. `block_spans` returns no span, but `block_body` returns the text between the two prose markers, `has_legacy_block` is true, and `_block_state` returns `STALE`; `rules_status` therefore reports an absent/removed section as stale instead of `NO_BLOCK`.

chunk_findings.detail: The `.ddflow/.gitignore` body ignores `index.db-*` but not the main SQLite database file `index.db`. On a fresh project where ddflow creates `.ddflow/index.db`, the generated `.ddflow/.gitignore` does not match that file, so the `git add .ddflow` step instructed by `init` can commit the derived index. That is precisely the condition the surrounding comment says must be avoided because a committed index can resurrect dead agents' leases; the pattern needs to cover `index.db` itself (e.g. `index.db` and `index.db-*`, or `index.db*`).

chunk_findings.detail: `local_edits_path` chooses a backup path by checking `candidate.exists()` and then later writing with `atomic_write`, but the check and the write are not atomic. If two `adopt`/`_upsert_block` invocations run concurrently on the same file that has hand edits, both can call `local_edits_path(path)` before either has written the aside. Since `path.name + ".local-edits"` does not yet exist in either process, both return the same aside path. The second `atomic_write(aside, path.read_bytes())` then overwrites the first process’s backup (or, if `atomic_write` is exclusive, raises `FileExistsError`), so the first invocation’s preserved hand edits are lost or the update crashes. The numbering logic is therefore not safe under the interleaving this function’s “numbered when taken” contract implies.

For a lesson titled `Use` and a summary bullet `**Useful** explanation`, `_norm(lead)` is `useful`, `_norm(title)` is `use`, `a.startswith(b)` is true, and the function returns `explanation`. The lead’s actual wording (`Useful`) is dropped even though the docstring explicitly says a lead that says something the title does not is kept.

chunk_findings.detail:
The extracted `status` is discarded except for a substring check for `supersed`; every other parsed status is reported as `accepted`. Given an ADR containing:

```markdown
## Status
proposed
```

`scan_decisions` stores `extra={"status": "accepted"}`, misrepresenting a proposed/deprecated/draft decision as an accepted one. The function has already read the real status but flattens it incorrectly.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer/_scan.py:scan_decisions

chunk_findings.detail: It reports missing dependencies for every item in `plan.found`, including completed or dispositioned items. Given a completed task with `done=True` and `needs=["missing"]`, the function appends a note claiming that the item needing `missing` will not be offered until the dependency is corrected. A completed task is not offered in the first place, so the note’s stated consequence is false and can send the operator to “fix” a dependency that cannot affect the live queue.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer/_scan.py:_flag_unresolvable_needs

chunk_findings.detail: `_fenced` only re-reads after an opener that is still open at EOF, so a stray fence opener is not ignored if a later same-character fence supplies a closing line. Given a file whose lines are: ` ``` `, `## Phase 1`, `- [ ] do thing`, ` ```py `, `code`, ` ``` `, the first opener is treated as open until the last line, so `_fenced` marks every line fenced. `_sections` therefore sees no `## Phase 1`, and the checkbox is treated as code text rather than a task. The docstring promises that a stray fence costs one line of structure, but here it costs the headings and checkboxes up to the next real fence.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer/_tables.py:_fenced

chunk_findings.detail: The negation guard is applied to the whole verdict string, not to the disposition marker that is negated. For a `**STATUS**:` line whose captured text is `DONE, NOT REOPENED` (or `CLOSED, NOT REOPENED`), the split does not separate on commas/semicolons, so `_NEGATED.search(verdict)` matches and the function returns live (`("", "")`) before checking that `DONE`/`CLOSED` makes the section closed. A section explicitly marked done/closed but “not reopened” therefore imports its open checkboxes as live work. The same whole-line live check also makes `CLOSED (NOT IN PROGRESS)` become hold rather than closed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer/_tables.py:_status_disposition

chunk_findings.detail: `_prose_globs` strips a line citation before stripping trailing punctuation, so a path with a line citation followed by punctuation is returned with the line number still attached. For example, given the prose token `` `ddflow/services/importer.py:123,` ``, `_LINE_SUFFIX` does not match because of the trailing comma, then `.rstrip(".,;:")` removes the comma, leaving `ddflow/services/importer.py:123`; because the token has more than one slash, the function appends that string as a repo path/glob. The intended path is `ddflow/services/importer.py`, so the function can emit an invalid path such as `...py:123` (or `...py:123)` when the citation is parenthesized).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer/_titles.py:_prose_globs

chunk_findings.detail: `_prose_needs` treats the phrase `not only requires` as a negation and therefore suppresses a real dependency. The `_PROSE_NEGATED` pattern matches `not` followed by up to two words and end-of-before, so for input `not only requires 160.C.2` the preceding window `not only ` matches, and the function returns no dependencies even though the prose explicitly says the task requires `160.C.2`. This is wrong because `not only` is a correlative conjunction (it affirms the requirement), not a negation like `does not require`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer/_titles.py:_prose_needs

chunk_findings.detail:
When a phase heading is nested under an ancestor heading that carries a STATUS line, the phase’s `extra["status"]` is not inherited. At each heading `heading_status` is reset to `None`, and `phase_found.extra["status"]` is populated only from that local variable. Given:

```markdown
## Session
**STATUS**: PARTIAL
### 159.A
- [x] done task
```

the `### 159.A` phase is created with `extra["status"]` as `None`; the ancestor `PARTIAL` remains only in `stack`, and done boxes force `disposition=("", "")`. The phase verdict that relies on `phase.extra["status"]` will treat the all-ticked phase as finished despite the section being `PARTIAL`. This contradicts the code’s own comment that a `## Session` STATUS line governs the `### 159.A` groups under it and that the section verdict has to be carried down.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/importer/_todo.py:scan_todos

chunk_findings.detail:
An explicit ACTIVE status inherited from the stack is not returned, so archive files incorrectly override it. Given an archived file containing:

```markdown
## Session X
**STATUS**: ACTIVE
- [ ] open task
```

`_status_disposition` records the explicit active status as `("", "")` in `stack`. `_box_disposition` finds it, but the guard `if inherited and inherited[0]:` is false for an active tuple, so control falls through to the archive fallback and returns `("hold", ...)`. The open task is held even though its nearest section explicitly says ACTIVE, whereas the surrounding comments state that `("", "")` is an explicit ACTIVE status that should override inherited/ancestor state.
